summary.tldr: Bans goods made with forced labour from being imported into Canada and lets the minister target suspect goods for extra checks.
what_it_does: Prohibits importing goods that are made wholly or partly by forced labour.
Lets the Minister of Foreign Affairs make a list of goods that are suspected of being made by forced labour, and name the producer, country, region, or both.
Requires importers of listed goods to give the Canada Border Services Agency the required information when a customs officer asks for it.
Lets customs officers detain goods for up to 90 days, or longer if regulations allow, to decide whether they were made by forced labour.
Makes the importer and the goods owner responsible for costs tied to detention, storage, transport, or disposal if the goods are imported in violation of the ban.
Makes related changes to the Customs Tariff and sets different coming-into-force dates for sections 8 and 9.
